findings.message: Guard clause now only checks the bounds of `index`. If `index` is `undefined`/`NaN`, both comparisons are false, so the early return is skipped and `items[undefined]` / `items[NaN]` yields `undefined`, then `.id` throws a TypeError. The requirement says readId must not throw for an out-of-range index; non-integer inputs (e.g. undefined, NaN) fall outside the guard and cause a crash. Also the tests for integer bounds still pass, so the bug is silent for invalid input. Use `if (!(index >= 0 && index < items.length)) return null;` or explicitly validate `Number.isInteger(index)`.
